https://www.barrons.com/articles/what-reviewers-are-saying-about-apples-new-iphone-xs-and-xs-max-1537287807 What Reviewers Are Saying About Apple’s New iPhone XS and XS Max By Sept. 18, 2018 12:23 p.m. ET Text Size David Marino-Nachison Sept. 18, 2018 12:23 p.m. ET
Reviewers have characterized the latest round of high-end smartphones as not-quite-revolutionary upgrades, and the newest phones from Apple (AAPL)— the XS and larger XS Max , with the comparatively inexpensive XR coming later this year—seem to fit that description.
And so while the Barron’s Next 50 company’s latest four-digit-price-tag, big-screen pocket computers don’t scream “BUY ME,” they’re also powerful machines that reviewers consider among the best phones available anywhere. Apple's biggest phone yet can be a bit unwieldy for those with smaller hands, so WSJ's Joanna Stern recruited NBA legend Gheorghe Muresan to help put the 6.5-inch iPhone's screen, camera and battery through the paces. Photo: Caitlin Faw/The Wall Street Journal
Does that mean the price makes sense ? That’s your call, but in the meantime we’ve collected viewpoints from a range of reviewers. And if you’d rather read about what they mean for the stock, we’ve got that too .
“They’re great phones,” wrote Lauren Goode for Wired . “Just don’t expect to feel the kind of feelings, as you’re sliding this phone out of your pocket or purse, that you’d get with a radically redesigned piece of hardware. As I used these new phones, I found myself struggling to define, exactly, what felt new about them. It’s there; you just have to dig deep.”
More reviews:
• The screen on the XS, CNBC’s Todd Hasleton wrote , is “a brilliant, colorful and sharp OLED display that supports next-gen HDR 4K video. It’s one of the best screens on the market, up there with the display on the Samsung Galaxy Note 9.”
Are they too big? the New York Times’ Brian X. Chen seemed to think so. Then he changed his mind.
“These devices spend a lot of time in your pocket and your hand, and there are often compromises in portability and comfort when the screens balloon in size,” he wrote. “For those reasons, I never liked the Plus phones, the line of iPhones that Apple introduced in 2014 with 5.5-inch screens. They felt impossible to use with one hand and far too bulky in a pocket. Newsletter Sign-up
“So it’s humbling to come to you now with another confession: The iPhone XS and the iPhone XS Max may be making me a convert to bigger smartphones.”
• The Verge’s Nilay Patel praised both phones’ speakers and battery life, among other things. He also noted the camera on the XS, though, in his estimation, a non-Apple phone still has the best camera around.
“The XS makes the X camera look terrible most of the time,” he wrote. “But we’ve been saying the best smartphone camera on the market is Google’s Pixel 2 for a year now, so that’s the standard to beat. And…I think the Pixel 2 still has a better camera than the iPhone XS.”
• For those prone to a bit of sticker shock—but also immune to a bit—Scott Stein of CNET suggests waiting for Apple to launch a cheaper alternative later this year.
“If you love bigger phones, why not wait for the iPhone XR? Apple has a new proposition this year: the middle-sized, 6.1-inch, more affordable iPhone XR, coming Oct. 26,” he wrote. “It has a less exciting, lower-resolution LCD display, but a display that is indeed larger than the regular iPhone X.” More About Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50
The WSJ’s Joanna Stern felt the same way . “Imagine Goldilocks only tested the cold and hot porridges and never found the one that was ‘just right,’” she wrote. “Her life might have been entirely different. That’s how I feel about testing the iPhone XS and XS Max—without the iPhone XR—for the past week.”
• But for some, when it comes to money, enough is enough, as Buzzfeed’s John Paczkowski wrote —though this could be said of more phones than just these: “When I tell my wife I might want to upgrade, she asks the price. Then she says, ‘Which do you like better, new phones or vacations?’”
